Figures carried forward from the original business-opportunity slide: 600,000 globally and 100,000 in the US. Race category, measurement period, unique-person basis, and underlying sources are unspecified. These figures require validation before investor or public-market use.

What these figures do—and do not—tell us

They illustrate the scale used in the original business framing. They do not establish a total addressable market, willingness to pay, active users, or revenue. The two geographic counts should not be added: the US is a geographic subset of the global framing.

06 / Human capital & social capital

A purpose needs capabilities.
Capabilities need people.

Human capital brings experience and skills. Social capital connects that capability to participants, specialist expertise, and execution.

The foundation we bring

Endurance experience.
Professional execution.

Two co-founders are ultramarathon runners and working professionals engaged with their communities.

Experience spans communication, marketing, technology, design, and deployment of enterprise-level solutions.

Understand the people in the story

Endurance-athlete access to define the initial customer group and participant pool.

Shape a relevant product

Sports nutrition expertise alongside product, engineering, and UX capability.

Support business development

Patent / IP legal support and seed-fundraising strategy as the business takes shape.

The task is to turn relevant connections into defined contributions—not to imply a team is already in place.
